newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lizhu buys bank shares, changes name.
newsitem.headline: Lizhu buys bank shares, changes name.

text.p: Zhuhai Special Economic Zone Lizhu Pharmaceutical Group Inc said on Wednesday it would buy 20 million shares of Zhuhai City United Bank Co Ltd at their face value price of one yuan per share.
A company statement said Lizhu had also changed its name to Livzon Pharmaceutical Group Inc.
The statement, issued by the firm's board of directors, said the acquired shares would represent 6.11 percent of the Zhuhai Bank's initial-phase registered capital of 327.55 million yuan.
The bank is a city cooperative bank.
The purchase would need the approval of shareholders, and a meeting was expected to be convened soon, a company official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The official said the company intended to buy the shares as a step into the financial industry and help fund-raising.
Bank officials were not immediatly available for comment.
The company changed its name to improve its image, the official said, deciding to take "Zhuhai SEZ" out of the full name because the company's business was no longer confined to the city of Zhuhai.
Livzon sounded more international, he added.
The Shenzhen stock exchange on Wednesday morning suspended trading in the company's shares on the announcement, an exchange statement said. Trading will resume in the afternoon, it said.
The company's B shares closed on Tuesday at HK$5.83 per share and A shares ended at 12.99 yuan.
